args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for money rounding (FIN-212)

round_money() docstring promised banker's rounding but the implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent ties round to
the nearest even cent, and unquote the import order stays consistent.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix money rounding to banker's rounding (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Summary

`round_money()` in `src/money.py` documented banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) per FIN-212, but the implementation actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This caused the nightly build to fail on `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.

## Change

- `src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ...)`.
- No other changes; no new dependencies.

## Behavior

Half-cent ties now round to the nearest even cent:

| Input | Before (HALF_UP) | After (HALF_EVEN) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2.675 | 2.68 | 2.68 |
| 2.665 | 2.67 | 2.66 |

## Verification

- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: **passed**.

## Notes

Merging to `main` requires code-owner approval, so this PR is ready for review rather than merged.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Root cause:** `round_money()` in `src/money.py` had a docstring promising banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212) but the body used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.

**Changes:**
- Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` from `main`.
- Updated `src/money.py` only: import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` and pass it to `quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ...)`. One-line behavioral change, no new dependencies, no test edits (the test was already correct).

**Verification:**
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` → passed.
- First PR attempt was rejected because the branch had fallen behind `main`. I merged the latest `main` into the branch (new commit `0a9452f727`), re-confirmed the fix and tests were intact after the merge, and re-ran CI: `ci-0002` → passed.

**Pull request:** [#101 — "Fix money rounding to banker's rounding (FIN-212)"](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101), open against `main`, reviewer requested from `alex`. It is awaiting code-owner approval — I did not merge, since merging to `main` requires code-owner sign-off.

One note for whoever lands it: since `2.675` and `2.665` are exact decimal literals, the test exercises true tie-breaking correctly. But if this function ever receives amounts produced through float arithmetic, ties can disappear before rounding — worth keeping inputs as `Decimal` end-to-end.
